title: Jelly Roll Morton's boasts and fallen fortunes
summary: Morton disliked Louis Armstrong, claimed to have invented jazz, argued at the Howard Theatre, had sold his diamond teeth, and wrote King Porter Stomp and other tunes.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: I went up there to talk with him, and he like bugged me

to death. "Yeah, I want you, man. Yeah, I'm going to get this band together around here, and I want you because I know you used to be with Joe, and I know Joe. Joe was a good man." I said, "Oh yeah, he was a good trumpet player." He said, "Oh yeah. But I don't like Louis, though." The guy couldn't even like Louis -- "Because he won't play none of my tunes." I said, "Well, I don't know about that." "Everybody else has got a band plays 'King Porter Stomp' but him." I said, "Well, maybe Louis don't want to play it!" He was like that, you know what I mean? He'd been a big man come down. He had gold diamonds in his teeth and all that shit. Got broke, had to take them out. So it kind of brought him down. At that time, a big band was coming to the Howard Theatre every week, and he'd go over there messing with them, and arguing and going on, you know what I mean -- talking loud. He's the one that invented Jazz. "I'm the one that invented Jazz." He never played no Jazz; he played Ragtime. He didn't play no Jazz. I never heard him playing but Ragtime. [SINGS] -- that kind of thing.
But he was up one time. And he wrote some good tunes.
He was up? What do you mean by that?
Up. I mean he was up in...
Oh, you mean in his career.
Yeah. He was a big man. I mean, he was a big man at one time. He was big way before King and them,

because he came to Chicago before King Oliver. So he wrote a lot of tunes. He wrote "The Hesitation Blues" and he wrote "King Porter Stomp" and he wrote "Milenberg Joys" and he wrote "The Pearls" and he wrote "Kansas City Stomp".
